modules.title: System design
modules.summary: The mechanisms every design is built from, taught as trade-offs with numbers, plus classic and AI-era design exercises and the real-world practice of design docs, postmortems and migrations.

modules.title: Software foundations
modules.summary: Python from two angles, TypeScript on Node, React with Next.js, Postgres, and AI coding tools with production discipline.

modules.title: APIs and enterprise integrations
modules.summary: Connecting a system to the customer's systems of record: HTTP, JSON and OAuth 2.0, webhooks and Kafka events, and integrating with or migrating off legacy systems.

modules.title: Identity and integration ops
modules.summary: The hands-on work of connecting a product to a customer: SSO with OIDC and SAML against Okta, Entra ID or Keycloak, provisioning, machine-to-machine API auth, file feeds over SFTP, and testing and debugging all of it with Postman, Newman, curl and a SAML tracer.

modules.title: Data platforms and pipelines
modules.summary: The data layer under ML and AI work: Spark, lakehouse and stores, feature stores, cleaning and linking messy records, Snowflake and Databricks, dbt.

modules.title: Workflow orchestration and durable execution
modules.summary: Turning steps into repeatable, retryable pipelines: Airflow for ML and for data (with Dagster), the ML-native orchestrators, and Temporal.

modules.title: The ML platform: clusters, GPUs and training
modules.summary: What MLOps adds to software delivery; Kubernetes and EKS as the substrate; experiment tracking; GPUs as cluster resources; multi-node training; scheduling and tenancy of a shared cluster.

modules.title: Model release engineering
modules.summary: From a trained artifact to a version in production: registry and versioning, evaluation gates, CI/CD for ML, GitOps and Terraform, staged rollouts.

modules.title: Model serving and inference
modules.summary: Models as reliable inference services: serving architecture, SageMaker, open-weight LLM engines (vLLM, SGLang), TensorRT-LLM and edge, and GPUs inside a customer's own environment.

modules.title: LLM application building blocks
modules.summary: What every LLM system is assembled from: the model and its hosted APIs, prompt and context engineering, structured outputs and tool calling, retrieval over private data (two angles).

modules.title: Agents and agentic workflows
modules.summary: Agentic systems designed, connected, kept running, measured and constrained: agent architectures, MCP, durable orchestration, evaluation, guardrails, LLMOps.

modules.title: AI agents on Google Cloud
modules.summary: The Google Cloud agent platform as a paved road: the product map and how to read its status, ADK, running and deploying agents, agent identity, gateway and registry, regulated-environment controls, then observability, retrieval, memory and a platform design capstone.

modules.title: Deploying into customer environments
modules.summary: Running a system in infrastructure the customer owns: their cloud accounts, containers and CI/CD, serverless, restricted networks, and the cost and latency profile of LLM systems.

modules.title: Operating in production
modules.summary: After it ships: observability (platform and agent traces), model monitoring and drift, SLOs and on-call, debugging and postmortems, security and compliance, autoscaling and cost.

modules.title: Delivery and platform practice
modules.summary: How work is scoped, written down, piloted and turned into a platform others use: the forward-deployed delivery model, scoping and design docs, ADRs, workflow mapping, pilots, golden paths, reusable tooling.
